zh: 在我们出现之前就已经存在一个金融系统了。

zh: 两个头发乱糟糟的斯坦福小孩到底怎么可能找到那些大券商没找到的市场需求呢?

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: is a platform for commercial activity.
zh: 是一个商业活动的平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you make something that is commercially competitive from space versus doing it on Earth?
zh: 你如何做出从太空来做、而不是在地球上做,还能在商业上有竞争力的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: I started looking much more closely at the idea of powering data centers.
zh: 我开始更近距离地研究为数据中心供电这个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was becoming clear that that was going to be the place where all the energy usage was going anyways.
zh: 越来越清楚的是,所有的能源消耗终归都会流向那里。

en: If you're on a rocket that's taking you to space, rather than just disposing of that rocket or trying to reuse it, what if you just used it basically as the heatsink?
zh: 如果你在一枚正带你进入太空的火箭上,与其直接丢弃那枚火箭或者试图复用它,不如基本上就把它当作散热器来用呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you got a bunch of metal there.
zh: 因为你那里有一大堆金属。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you put these two ideas together, you arrive at the architecture that we have, which is that the upper stage of the rocket is itself the data center.
zh: 而当你把这两个想法放在一起时,就得出了我们现在拥有的架构,那就是火箭的上面级本身就是数据中心。

zh: 我是 Juven,Kleiner Perkins 的合伙人。在这档节目中,我们会超越高光集锦,深入探讨打造创造历史的公司过程中个人与职业上的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today on Grit, I'm talking with Baiju Bhatt, co-founder of Robinhood and now founder and CEO of Cowboy Space.
zh: 今天在 Grit 节目中,我和 Baiju Bhatt 对谈,他是 Robinhood 的联合创始人,现在是 Cowboy Space 的创始人兼 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: Baiju helped build Robinhood from a controversial idea into a public company worth tens of billions and then did the least obvious thing imaginable.
zh: Baiju 帮助把 Robinhood 从一个备受争议的想法打造成了一家价值数百亿美元的上市公司,然后做了一件最难以想象的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: He walked away from the executive seat and started a rocket company.
zh: 他离开了高管席位,创办了一家火箭公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We get into what it's actually like to start over from zero as a repeat founder, why he seeded it with his own money to beam power and AI compute down from orbit, and the pivot that turned a space solar startup into one of the fastest growing unicorns in the space industry.
zh: 我们聊到了作为一位连续创始人从零重新开始究竟是什么感觉、他为什么用自己的钱种子轮投资这家从轨道向地面传输电力和 AI 算力的公司,以及那次转型——把一家太空太阳能初创公司变成了太空行业中增长最快的独角兽之一。

en: I really genuinely have.

en: When...

en: Yeah.

en: Yeah, geez.

en: 14 years?

en: And it's all real, too.

speaker: Unknown
en: That's good.

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you think...

speaker: Unknown
en: It was your life's work until the very end, or I'm curious, like your metamorphosis of, you know, 14 years is a really long time.
zh: 它一直是你毕生的事业直到最后吗?还是说,我很好奇,你知道,14 年真的很长。

en: I'm very curious how your relationship to-

speaker: Unknown
en: Robin Hood, I don't know.

en: Like, was that always your calling?

en: I'm just really curious how that like metamorphosized for you.
zh: 我真的很好奇这对你来说是怎么样演变过来的。

en: I'm not a finance guy.
zh: 我不是搞金融的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I'm not, you know?
zh: 真的不是,你懂的?

en: And just very candidly, like my background is in physics and math.
zh: 而且非常坦白地说,我的背景是物理和数学。

en: And going to Stanford, studying physics and math, for a long time I thought I wanted to be an academic mathematician or an academic physicist.
zh: 在斯坦福学习物理和数学期间,很长时间里我都以为自己想成为一名学院派的数学家或者学院派的物理学家。

en: I wanted to study string theory.

en: I wanted to understand

en: Do you know what this is, by the way?

speaker: Unknown
en: Not the nature of grand unification.
zh: 不是大统一的本质。

speaker: Unknown
en: But do you know about the grand unified theory?
zh: 但你知道大统一理论吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you heard this before?
zh: 你以前听说过吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Please, please.
zh: 请讲,请讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's this idea that there is one theory to rule them all, right?
zh: 就是这么一个想法:存在一个统领一切的理论,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the love of this stuff, honestly, I have a lot of credit to give my dad to.
zh: 而我觉得,说实话,对这些东西的热爱,我很大程度上要归功于我爸。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's also a physicist by training.
zh: 他也是科班出身的物理学家。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this idea that there's a grand theory to rule them all, and there's a lot of breadcrumbs in our understanding of physics that would point to that being not just possible, but...
zh: 但这个「有一个统领一切的大理论」的想法,而且我们对物理学的理解中有很多线索指向这不仅是可能的,而且……

speaker: Unknown
en: It's plausible or even likely to be the case.
zh: 是说得通的,甚至很可能是事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have the standard model of particle physics that unifies electromagnetism, strong force and weak force, and then there's the outlier, which is gravity.
zh: 所以你有粒子物理的标准模型,它统一了电磁力、强力和弱力,然后还有那个离群者,就是引力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the pursuit of a quantum theory of gravity are like, and what is the real nature of gravity when you get to the finest scale resolution?
zh: 所以对量子引力理论的追求,比如说,在最精细的尺度分辨率下引力的真正本质是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the kind of stuff I was interested in when I was in school.
zh: 那是我在上学时感兴趣的那类东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I kind of, I remember pretty early on in my professional career telling myself, if I ever hit a big of this finance thing, I'm gonna start a space company someday.
zh: 所以我有点……我记得在我职业生涯很早期就跟自己说,如果我在这个金融行当里捞到一大笔,我总有一天要开一家太空公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I guess that's not directly- Are you serious?
zh: 我想这并不直接……你是认真的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or you just, is this the retrospective- No, no, no.
zh: 还是你只是……这是事后回顾吗……不,不,不。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was very, very actively thinking about this.
zh: 我当时是非常、非常主动地在想这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: While at Robin Hood.
zh: 在 Robin Hood 的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: While at Robin Hood, yeah.
zh: 在 Robin Hood 的时候,是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm reminded of this sometimes when I hang out with early Robin Hood people where I'm like, did I talk about space stuff back then?
zh: 有时候我和早期 Robin Hood 的老人聚会时就会想起来,我会问,我那时候是不是聊过太空的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: And people are like, Beijou, that was like either the second or the third thing you would say back in the day.
zh: 大家会说,Baiju,那当年是你张口就说出来的第二件或第三件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had always been, I guess, space and pure theoretical physics are not the same thing, but the love of pure theoretical physics, which is kind of what my academic background is, I couldn't kind of keep it at bay.
zh: 我一直是……我想,太空和纯理论物理不是一回事,但对纯理论物理的热爱,这大概是我的学术背景,我没办法把它按下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: So even in the companies before Robin Hood, I remember Vlad and I would stay up into the wee hours of the night programming and then at like...
zh: 所以即使在 Robin Hood 之前的那些公司里,我记得 Vlad 和我会熬夜编程到深夜,然后在大概……

speaker: Unknown
en: Three o'clock in the morning when we were just like a little bit like, you know, a little sleep deprived, we'd be like, you know, it'd be cool, see if we could mine helium-3 on the moon.
zh: 凌晨三点的时候,我们有点……你知道,有点睡眠不足,我们就会说,你知道,要是能去月球上采氦-3 该多酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we would like talk about this stuff all the time.
zh: 我们会一直聊这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm rambling here a little bit, but I remember in high school, my high school chemistry teacher gave me a copy of this book, The Case for Mars.
zh: 我这里有点跑题了,但我记得高中时,我的高中化学老师给了我一本书,《The Case for Mars》(火星的缘由)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you heard of this before?
zh: 你以前听说过这本书吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, you should, I have a stack of them in my office, I'll give one to you.
zh: 好的,你应该了解一下,我办公室里有一摞,我会送你一本。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't read it right when my high school teacher gave it to me.
zh: 我高中老师给我的时候我并没有马上读。

speaker: Unknown
en: I read it a little bit later on in life, but it left quite an impression on me.
zh: 我是后来人生中稍晚一点才读的,但它给我留下了相当深的印象。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what this book is, I believe it's also the blueprint for what would become SpaceX, but it's a path towards...
zh: 这本书讲的是……我相信它也是后来 SpaceX 的蓝图,它是一条通往……

speaker: Unknown
en: The book was written by one of the scientists that worked with Papa Bush, President Papa Bush.
zh: 这本书的作者之一是曾为老布什、老布什总统工作过的科学家。

speaker: Unknown
en: When he first got elected, he had this thing, if I remember correctly, it was like the 100-day plan, right?
zh: 在他刚当选的时候,我记得他有一个东西,好像是叫百日计划,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: 100 days to build a plan to go to Mars.
zh: 用一百天制定一个去火星的计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think as every president during that era was like, you know, we're gonna do space.
zh: 我想那个时代的每一任总统都是那样,你知道的,我们要搞太空。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, get me the best scientists, get me a plan.
zh: 就像,给我找最好的科学家,给我一个计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they make this plan, and the plan is basically like, step one, build Battlestar Galactica.
zh: 然后他们做了这个计划,这个计划基本上就是:第一步,建造太空堡垒卡拉狄加。

speaker: Unknown
en: Step two, build a moon base.
zh: 第二步,建一个月球基地。

speaker: Unknown
en: Step three, fly Battlestar Galactica to the moon base.
zh: 第三步,把太空堡垒卡拉狄加飞到月球基地。

speaker: Unknown
en: Come on.
zh: 拜托。

speaker: Unknown
en: Step four, go to Mars.
zh: 第四步,去火星。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I'm, you know...
zh: 我是说,你知道……

speaker: Unknown
en: Adding some color here, but like the whole thing was gonna cost like a, you know, a hundred zillion dollars to do, making up some numbers here.
zh: 我在这里加了一些渲染,但整个计划大概要花,你知道,一万亿亿美元,这里我是在编数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the book was born of one of the scientists that worked on this and was basically like, look, if you actually wanna go to Mars, this is not how you would do it.
zh: 但这本书出自参与这个计划的其中一位科学家之手,基本上就是说:听着,如果你真想去火星,这不是你会用的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you actually wanted to go to Mars, you would take an engineering approach to it, right?
zh: 如果你想真的去火星,你会用工程学的方法来做,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Where you would
zh: 你会

speaker: Unknown
en: Like look for reusable components.
zh: 比如寻找可复用的部件。

speaker: Unknown
en: You would look to down cost stuff.
zh: 你会想着去削减成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: You would look to find ways to sort of build this stuff closer to what it actually costs versus what the government spends on these things.
zh: 你会想着去找各种办法，让制造这些东西的成本更接近它的实际成本，而不是政府花在这些东西上的钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's kind of what this thesis, that's kind of the core thesis of this book, The Case from Mars.
zh: 而这差不多就是这个论点，差不多就是这本书《The Case from Mars》的核心论点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to kind of come full circle, I remember reading that and being like, man, like, if this is possible, I really want to...
zh: 然后说回来，我记得读那本书的时候，我心想，天哪，如果这是可能的，我真的想要……

speaker: Unknown
en: See if I can do that at some point in my professional career.
zh: 看看我能不能在我职业生涯的某个阶段做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then obviously the backdrop as I was building Robinhood of seeing SpaceX land the reusable rocket for the first time.
zh: 然后显然，在我构建 Robinhood 的那个背景下，我看到了 SpaceX 第一次让可回收火箭着陆。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, oh my goodness, if this is happening in my lifetime and I don't, and I'm not a part of this.
zh: 我当时想，我的天哪，如果这在我有生之年发生了，而我没有参与其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like this is one of the few things that as an old man, I'm gonna look back and like fundamentally regret.
zh: 这是极少数我老了以后回头看会从根本上感到后悔的事情之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I had actually been thinking about building a space company for a long time.
zh: 所以其实我很长一段时间以来一直在考虑创建一家太空公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Didn't know if I was actually gonna do it or not, but there was, you know, the idea had been pulling on my heartstrings for a very long time.
zh: 不知道自己是否真的会去做，但你知道，这个想法已经撩拨我的心弦很久了。

en: Well, this might sound like a weird question, but the way you said, like, I'm not a finance guy talking about your work at Robin Hood,
zh: 好吧，这听起来可能是个奇怪的问题，但你说“我不是搞金融的人”的那种方式，在谈到你在 Robin Hood 的工作时，

speaker: Unknown
en: It gives me the impression that there was, I don't know if like it's like hollow about the mission.
zh: 给我的印象是，我不知道是不是像使命里有什么空洞的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, quite the opposite.
zh: 其实恰恰相反。

speaker: Unknown
en: The mission was around changing the status quo, right?
zh: 使命就是关于改变现状，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: The whole point of the company was and continues to be to democratize finance for all, right?
zh: 这家公司的全部意义过去是、现在仍然是让所有人都能享受金融民主化，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a challenger mission in many ways, right?
zh: 从很多方面来说，这是一个挑战者的使命，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like saying that the system...
zh: 就像是在说，这个系统……

speaker: Unknown
en: When we started was not what we thought what it should be.
zh: 当我们开始的时候，并不是我们认为它应该成为的样子。

en: And we thought it should be one that includes more people, right?
zh: 而我们认为它应该是一个包容更多人的系统，对吧？

en: One that lowers the barriers to entry so that it isn't just institutional investors or extraordinarily high net worth people that are using the stock market.

speaker: Unknown
en: So the mission very much resonated with me, but the mission was one of changing the status quo.
zh: 所以这个使命非常能引起我的共鸣，但这个使命是关于改变现状的。

en: Yeah.

en: Yeah.
